title: Lessons Learned: Wifi Server Disaster
why_read: A lighthearted personal anecdote about a home server accidentally running on WiFi instead of ethernet, offering relatable but low technical substance.
analysis: The post describes a common home-lab mistake: a self-hosted server staying on WiFi because ethernet cabling and switch configuration were never finished, leading to a service outage when connectivity dropped. There's no deep technical content here beyond basic networking common sense and a reminder to monitor uptime and not let free-tier monitoring lapse. It reads as a casual, relatable story rather than something offering new engineering insight.
